comparison: Both address the cryo-EM structure and asymmetric dimer architecture (C3, C4, C34-C39, C53-C55). OpenEval finds the structural data SUPPORTED at 3.7Å resolution with clear domain arrangements. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, explicitly challenging the resolution quality: 'You can't reliably report the presence of a hydrogen bond with a 3.7Å resolution' and criticizing insufficient data processing information. Major disagreement on structural interpretation reliability.

Both evaluate TPRA/PHA-KDB interactions and activation segment stabilization (C5, C56-C57, C59-C62, C64, C67, C74-C75). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with clear structural evidence for active kinase conformation. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, specifically questioning hydrogen bond claims (C60, C64) at 3.7Å resolution and noting the C-terminal truncation limitation affects physiological relevance.

Both address HDX-MS data showing TRX1-induced allosteric changes (C6-C8, C93-C94, C97-C101, C107, C120, C128-C131, C133). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with significant protection patterns and systematic changes across domains. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, stating 'The evidence of ASK1 interaction with TRX1 is compelling' and accepting HDX-MS as compensation for lack of complex structure. Strong agreement.

Both evaluate TRX1 binding site identification via HDX-MS (C95-C96, C108-C110). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with protection of TRX1 active site and overlap with NMR data. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED as part of the overall compelling TRX1 interaction evidence. Agreement on HDX-MS binding site data.

Both address HDX-MS changes in KD regions and PH-KD linker upon TRX1 binding (C102-C106). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with clear reduced deuteration and structural correlation. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED as part of the convincing allosteric mechanism evidence. Agreement on these specific HDX-MS findings.

Both evaluate whether TRX1 disrupts ASK1 dimerization (C134-C135). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN, noting HDX-MS shows altered but not disrupted interactions, with acknowledged uncertainty at physiological concentrations. Peer reviewers rate the overall HDX-MS findings SUPPORTED but do not specifically address the dimerization question, accepting the authors' interpretation.

Both address AUC data on domain contributions to dimerization (C77-C82, C89-C90). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with clear sedimentation data showing progressive dimerization stability. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, acknowledging 'SV AUC and HDX-MS techniques to compensate for the inability to get a sufficiently stable ASK1:TRX complex' as acceptable. Agreement on AUC findings.

Both evaluate AUC data on TRX1 effects on ASK1 oligomerization (C91-C92). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with appropriate caveats about physiological concentrations. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, implicitly accepting these findings as part of the overall convincing evidence. Agreement on AUC oligomerization data.

Both address interpretation of dimerization mechanisms from AUC and structure (C84-C88). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED as logical structure-function correlation. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED without specific criticism of these interpretations. Agreement on mechanistic interpretation.

Both evaluate TBD structural features including thioredoxin-like fold and flexibility (C40-C43, C45, C47-C50). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with clear structural evidence. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN due to overall resolution concerns but do not specifically challenge TBD structural claims. Partial disagreement based on general resolution skepticism.

Both address CRR structure comparison with isolated crystal structure (C51-C52). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with documented similarities and minor differences. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN due to overall structural quality concerns but do not specifically critique this comparison. Implicit disagreement on reliability.

Both evaluate KD dimer interface and asymmetry (C58, C63, C65-C66, C68-C73). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with well-resolved interface and appropriate structural comparisons. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, challenging specific interaction claims at 3.7Å resolution and noting C-terminal truncation limitations. Disagreement on interpretation certainty.

Both address interpretive claims about N-terminal interactions, CC motif role, TPR flexibility, and T838 stabilization (C111-C113, C116, C121-C122). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN, noting speculative nature and lack of direct validation. Peer reviewers also rate UNCERTAIN, explicitly citing C-terminal truncation as limiting certainty about activation mechanisms. Agreement on uncertainty.

Both address background claims about ASK1 biology and regulation (C1-C2, C9-C33). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED as established literature. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, implicitly accepting the biological context without criticism. Agreement on background information.

Both evaluate citations to prior work on ASK1 and related systems (C117-C119, C123-C127, C132). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED as appropriate contextualization. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED without questioning these literature references. Agreement on background citations.

Both address speculative claims about 14-3-3, TRAF/Daxx, limitations, and therapeutic implications (C136-C143). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN, noting speculative nature with appropriate caveats. Peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED, explicitly endorsing therapeutic potential: 'will greatly contribute to the development of new drugs targeting ASK1.' Disagreement on acceptance of forward-looking statements.

OpenEval addresses resolution and data deposition as factual statements (C144-C145), rating SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers question the 3.7Å resolution quality and criticize lack of data processing information, rating structural claims UNCERTAIN. Disagreement on whether resolution is adequate for reported interpretations.
